unit.title: Fractions and Percentages
unit.blurb: Fractions as division, finding fractions of amounts, percentages of shapes and amounts, and comparing fractions, decimals and percentages.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand that a fraction can be a division (3/4 = 3 ÷ 4), and find fractions of quantities.

O2.t: Understand percentages as parts of 100 and find simple percentages of quantities.

O3.t: Recognise equivalent fractions, decimals and percentages, and compare and order them.

p: 3/4 means **3 ÷ 4**. If 3 pizzas are shared equally between 4 people, each person gets 3/4 of a pizza.
The **denominator** (bottom) shows how many equal parts; the **numerator** (top) shows how many parts we have.
To find 3/5 of 40: divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, then 8 × 3 = **24**.
To find 2/3 of 12, do 12 ÷ 3 = 4 then × 2 = 8. Do not divide by 2.

p: **Per cent** means 'out of 100'. 37% means 37 out of 100. On a **100 square**, 37% is 37 of the small squares.
50% = half, 25% = a quarter, 10% = a tenth, 1% = a hundredth.
Use 10% to build others: 10% of 60 = 6, so 30% = 18 and 5% = 3.
If 35% of a class are boys, 65% are girls (35 + 65 = 100).

p: **Equivalent fractions** have the same value: multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12.
To compare fractions, change them to the same denominator or to decimals: 3/5 = 0.6 and 2/3 ≈ 0.67, so 3/5 < 2/3.
1/8 is smaller than 1/5: the more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part is.
